$comment: #EXP-2138 (Danny, 2026-11-25): DELETING REMOVES THE TRANSCRIPT. What a device keeps of a chat (its run record, journal and diff sidecar, scratch dir, its rows of the chat store) is removed by deleting the chat, its agent or its team, and by nothing else here: ending, archiving, moving (device, Assistant, group chat) or trashing a board keeps it, and a row missing from sync or from a read never removes anything (the other removers are the machine's `Keep session history` window and a deliberate sign-out of the chat store). SERVER: `sessions.heldGone {ids: uuid[] (at most limits.batch)}` (POST) -> `{gone: uuid[]}`, a person's login only (an `expu_` key, an MCP call or an agent gets FORBIDDEN). heldByCaller(row, caller): an id is KEPT when its row exists and the caller STARTED it (no membership needed), or is a member of its team and it is `shared`, or OWNS a device row of the machine the row names (whoever may read it: a shared box runs teammates' private chats). Else it is gone; unknown and forbidden answer the same. `serverCases`. THE SIGNAL: the delete itself (`sessions.delete`, `agents.delete`, `teams.delete`, the admin's and the import sweep's team delete) sends every session of the deleted trees, live or not, `kill {sessionId, reason: "deleted"}` down its device's control socket, after the commit, the targets read before it. An older relay or client drops `reason` (an ordinary kill). DEVICE (desktop app and CLI daemon), per account (its id names the instance and the user, so another login never shares state): candidates = the session ids of the account's run records (repo-backed too; a `/btw` aside is no session of the server) and of its chat store (roots and sessions), uuids only (`candidateCases`). It asks once signed in and synced, then every limits.askEveryHours; a notice asks at once, for the noticed ids only. heldPass({now (ms), holds, asked, gone (null = the whole ask failed, was refused or did not parse: nothing changes), state {id: {first, last}}, notices}) -> {remove, state, notices, capped}: an asked id NOT answered gone loses its first answer and its notice; a gone one with a notice is removed at once; any other gone one stores the answer's time (`first`, `last`) durably and is removed by an answer at least limits.confirmHours after `first`; `now` before `last` (the clock went backwards) starts over. A notice alone removes nothing. Only asked ids count. CAP: more than limits.capCount removals (noticed ids exempt) that are more than half of `holds` remove nothing but the noticed ones; the first answers stay. State and notices of ids no longer held are dropped; a removed id keeps its entry until its files are really gone (the host clears it). A run live here is ended first; while it lives nothing of it is removed (the next pass tries again). `passCases`. REMOVED (`removeCases`): this account's run record, its scratch dir (only when no other record names it; a repo worktree is never touched), the journal + diff sidecar when the record is this account's, or when no record names it, this account's chat store does and no other account's on this machine does; the chat store's messages, events, docs and tools of the session. A journal no account can be tied to stays. Mirrors: TS src/held-gone.ts, desktop `domain::held_gone` (host half `steer::held_gone`); the phones and the web hold no run records.
